Research Project

Dynamic Forest Governance & Biodiversity Policy Analytics

The project models forest biomass, biodiversity, and cumulative harvesting pressure as jointly evolving states. Biodiversity contributes directly to biomass productivity, while past harvesting creates an ecological-memory channel through cumulative pressure.

Three governance regimes are compared over a finite horizon: a noncooperative open-loop Nash benchmark with free terminal states, cooperative regulation with fixed ecological targets, and cooperative regulation with free terminal states. Disturbance exposure enters as a deterministic expected biodiversity-loss drift rather than as realized stochastic shocks.

Policy Diagnostic

Shadow-Value Wedge

The biomass shadow-value wedge τ(t) = λReg(t) − λOLNE(t) measures the model-implied gap between cooperative and decentralized marginal valuation of standing biomass.

Policy Reading

What the Model Supports

The model identifies incentive direction and timing; it does not estimate an implementable tax rate or a complete policy package.

  • Harvest incentives: a positive biomass-value wedge signals under-valuation of standing biomass in decentralized harvesting.
  • Target-based regulation: fixed ecological endpoints meet prescribed terminal states but can require stronger late-horizon adjustments.
  • Adaptive cooperation: free-terminal regulation produces smoother adjustment and the strongest biodiversity recovery in the baseline.
  • Instrument families: harvest charges, conservation subsidies, payments for ecosystem services, and performance-based conservation mechanisms are consistent with the paper's policy discussion.

Baseline Comparison

Decision Metrics

Current-scenario terminal states, harvest metrics, and model objectives. Parentheses report the change from the published baseline.

Objective values retain the manuscript's definitions: OLNE is discounted profit per agent, while cooperative values are regulator totals including ecological valuation. They should not be interpreted as directly comparable market revenues.
Real-World Application

From Model Diagnostics to Forest Policy

Concession & harvest planningUse regime comparisons to examine how decentralized extraction incentives alter biomass, biodiversity, and cumulative pressure.
PES / conservation financeUse shadow-value differences as a structured diagnostic for where incentive alignment may be needed; monetary implementation requires external calibration.
Adaptive managementUse sensitivity results to identify which ecological parameters deserve stronger monitoring and which governance designs exhibit stronger endpoint effects.
Deployment requirement: a real forest-management application should recalibrate timber prices, harvest costs, biodiversity indices, disturbance exposure, ecological growth parameters, monitoring quality, and enforcement constraints to the target forest. The current dashboard is a validated analytical implementation of the published calibration, not a forecast for a specific forest concession.
Computational validation. Baseline and scenario trajectories were independently reconstructed from the Appendix C equations using a boundary-value solver. The terminal states and control paths reproduce the published benchmark patterns, and the sensitivity explorer uses independently re-solved one-at-a-time parameter scenarios at −20%, −10%, 0%, +10%, and +20%.
